extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal. It evaluates the capacity of LLMs to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. The dataset contains 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world scenarios (conference, organization, education, and game domains) across over 1373 webpages. It includes both single-source and multi-source QA types to simulate different human web-navigation paradigms.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The collection pipeline involves: (1) Traversing official websites recursively, collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages; (2) Constructing queries based on the provided page information and specified role, such as focusing on the solo page or considering both pages simultaneously; (3) Verifying and filtering for legitimate queries that deviate from natural, human-like phrasing, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Root official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. The root page is initially identified through a Google search using keywords such as 'conference official website' or 'game official website', followed by manual filtering. For the education domain, official websites of various university computer science departments were chosen.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Web pages' markdown content along with clickable HTML buttons (and corresponding URL) extracted using Beautiful Soup. The data construction includes both multi-source and single-source types, corresponding to two types of human information-seeking behaviours within web pages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o performs initial annotations, followed by a second stage where crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering to refine the final results. Human annotators rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure the QA pairs are correct and consistent.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: After the synthetic queries are generated by LLM, human annotators can rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure the QA pairs are correct and consistent.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be available at HuggingFace Datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset Size: Due to the complexity of queries in the web-agent domain, WebWalkerQA currently comprises 680 high-quality QA pairs. Additionally, approximately 14k silver QA pairs exist, which, although not yet carefully human-verified, can serve as supplementary training data. Multimodal Environment: Only HTML-DOM is utilized to parse clickable buttons; visual modalities such as screenshots are not included.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing, Validation. The benchmark is designed to evaluate the ability of LLMs to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website. WebWalkerQA focuses on text-based reasoning abilities, using a Question-Answer format to evaluate traversal and problem-solving capabilities in web scenarios.
